name: Where medicine meets machine learning: A doctor's story of dual passions

content.title: Where medicine meets machine learning: A doctor's story of dual passions
content.summary: Dr Andai's passionate journey to data science

media.alt: Where medicine meets machine learning: A doctor's story of dual passions

content.text: Dr. David Andai is a young doctor who is carving out a unique path that merges medicine with data science. Starting with a childhood love for technology, his journey led him to the Brain and Mind Institute, where he is making strides in brain health. In this Q&A, Dr. Andai shares how his passion for IT and medicine converged, what motivates him, and his vision for the future of healthcare. He also reflects on the mentors and milestones that have shaped his career.

I am a bit of a wild card-naturally inclined to lead, plan, and dive deep into challenges. But at heart, I am still that curious kid, playful and eager to explore. I am a doctor by training, with a degree from JKUAT University, but my true passion lies in research, especially in the lab where I can work with data and make a real impact.
Can you share your journey from being an intern to becoming a Research Assistant at the Brain and Mind Institute? What were the key milestones and experiences that shaped your path?

My journey at the Brain and Mind Institute (BMI) started when my mentor, Dr. Beverly Cheserem, introduced me to Dr Rachel Maina during the 2023 Healing the Brain conference hosted by BMI. The environment at BMI instantly resonated with me, and I was eager to be a part of it. As an intern, I was involved in the Uzima-DS project, where I worked on data aspects and developed new skills in building dashboards and presenting data insights. The teamwork and support at BMI were crucial in my growth, leading to my current role as a Research Assistant.
As a medical doctor, what drew you to data science and machine learning?

My love for computers began in grade 3, and even though I pursued medicine at my parents' urging, I always felt a pull toward IT and design. The COVID-19 pandemic gave me the chance to explore data science, and I realized its potential to revolutionize healthcare. I became passionate about the intersection of medicine, user experience design, and data science, seeing it as a way to transform patient care.
What does your role at the Uzima-DS project involve?

I joined Uzima-DS when the focus on data was intensifying. My role involves ensuring data quality, producing reports, and providing insights from data analysis. Working with wearable tech and mental health data is especially rewarding, offering both challenges and opportunities for innovation.
What are your career goals in medical data analysis and machine learning?

In the short term, I want to deepen my knowledge in data science, particularly in brain and mental health, and mentor others in healthcare who are interested in data. Long term, I envision applying machine learning to healthcare, especially in brain-computer interface technologies, to tackle critical issues in neuroscience and psychiatry.
What keeps you motivated in this field?

Curiosity drives me. The unpredictability of where my work might lead keeps me engaged. My passion for design and data analysis grows with continuous learning, and I am excited to see where it will take me.

I encourage early-career medics to think differently and explore new paths. Don't be limited by tradition-find what excites you and pursue it passionately. Embrace the chaos and seize the opportunities it brings.
